claims.text: The starting material is a high-entropy alloy in the as-cast state.
Machine-learning prediction of phase diagrams can identify an optimal alloy composition.
Changing the alloy to the machine-learning-selected composition will enhance thermal conductivity.
Enhanced thermal conductivity will improve heat-transfer capability.
The composition change will preserve structural integrity.
Heat-transfer capability will improve by 15% relative to current intermediate-layer performance.
The predicted improvement and preservation of structural integrity will hold at temperatures up to 1000°C.
The predicted improvement and preservation of structural integrity will hold under loading up to 100 MPa.
The optimized and baseline compositions will be compared in a plasma-facing reactor component simulator under the stated temperature and loading conditions.
The hypothesis is falsified if heat-transfer capability improves by less than 10% relative to baseline.
The hypothesis is falsified if hardness or toughness decreases by more than 5%.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome is a 15% improvement, but the experiment only falsifies the hypothesis below 10%; an observed improvement from 10% to under 15% would fail to achieve the stated prediction without falsifying it.
